title: BMW, the maker of sporty cars, is now available to you
what: BMW of Munich builds sporty saloons, the 3, 5 and 7 Series, and motorcycles. It sold 339,232 cars in 1980. The Quandt family saved the company from bankruptcy in 1959 and is still its largest shareholder; Eberhard von Kuenheim has run it since 1970. BMW is much smaller than Daimler-Benz but has grown quickly.
why: The listing beat. The arc: the boom years of the 1980s, the Rover disaster of 1994-2000, the 'premium only' recovery with Mini and Rolls-Royce, and the China slump of the 2020s.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (sales table, Quandt 1959, read 2026-10-03); https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eberhard_von_Kuenheim (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW launches the new 3 Series
what: BMW released the second generation of its compact 3 Series at the end of November. For the first time it will also come as a four-door saloon, so that it suits families, not only enthusiasts.
why: The E30 became BMW's volume pillar of the 1980s and carried the growth that made the share a star of the decade. [Lookahead review: estate version (1987) named in 1982.]
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_3_Series_(E30) (read 2026-10-03)

title: A BMW engine wins the Formula One title
what: Nelson Piquet won the Formula One drivers' championship on 15 October in South Africa, two points ahead of Alain Prost. His Brabham ran on a BMW turbocharged engine; it is the first title won with a turbo.
why: Image beat for the sporty brand in a year when German car shares soared.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Formula_One_World_Championship (read 2026-10-03)

title: Foreign buyers send BMW shares soaring
what: Foreign investors have discovered German shares, reacting late to the good economic news and rising profits of big German companies. Daimler reached new record highs this month after three years of rising prices, and BMW and Porsche shares made unusually large gains.
why: Start of BMW's best twelve months in the game (+115% from April 1985 to April 1986); about 4 points of the month's +25% came from the falling dollar.
source: Die Zeit, 'Börsen-Report: Daimler ist Spitze', 30 August 1985, https://www.zeit.de/1985/36/daimler-ist-spitze (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW jumps 40% as foreign money returns
what: After a weak spring, German shares rose again in August on orders from abroad; foreign investors are betting on a further rise of the mark and on lower interest rates, and by the end of the month the market was close to its April record. BMW, which raised new capital in July with a rights issue, rose fastest. Its new 7 Series luxury saloon has been in production since June.
why: +40% (about +34% in marks), BMW's biggest month in the game; the boom ended with the crash of October 1987.
source: Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Aktien schlagen Renten', 22 August 1986, https://www.zeit.de/1986/35/aktien-schlagen-renten (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Bank und Börse: Käufer kehren zurück', 29 August 1986, https://www.zeit.de/1986/36/kaeufer-kehren-zurueck (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_7_Series_(E32) (read 2026-10-03); data/manual/bmw.csv header (rights issue 4:1 of 28 July 1986) (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW starts building the Z1 roadster
what: BMW began production of the Z1 in October, a two-seat roadster with plastic body panels and doors that slide down into the body. It was unveiled at the Frankfurt motor show in 1987; by the start of production the price had risen above the original target of 80,000 marks.
why: A small image car in a quiet year after the crash; its mass-produced successor, the Z3, followed in 1995.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_Z1 (read 2026-10-03)

title: The Gulf crisis ends the reunification boom
what: Since Iraq invaded Kuwait on 2 August, oil prices have jumped and stock markets have been falling worldwide. After the boom in German shares that followed the opening of the Berlin Wall, investors are now selling. BMW lost more than a fifth of its value in September.
why: Gulf crisis sell-off; BMW recovered in October (+13%) and February 1991 (+21%) as the war ended.
source: Die Zeit, 'Aktien haben ihren Reiz verloren', 17 August 1990, https://www.zeit.de/1990/34/aktien-haben-ihren-reiz-verloren (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Verkaufsdruck aus London', 31 August 1990, https://www.zeit.de/1990/36/verkaufsdruck-aus-london (read 2026-10-03); data/out/bmw.json (read 2026-10-03)

title: Hopes of peace in the Gulf lift shares
what: Stock markets rose in February as the Gulf war neared its end, after Iraq said it was ready, under conditions, to leave Kuwait.
why: +21% for BMW, a relief rally after the Gulf-crisis lows of autumn 1990.
source: Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Spekulation auf Frieden', 22 February 1991, https://www.zeit.de/1991/09/spekulation-auf-frieden (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Jubel-Hausse blieb aus', 1 March 1991, https://www.zeit.de/1991/10/jubel-hausse-blieb-aus (read 2026-10-03); data/out/bmw.json (read 2026-10-03)

title: Bernd Pischetsrieder takes over from von Kuenheim
what: Eberhard von Kuenheim handed over the chairmanship of BMW on 13 May after 23 years and moves to the supervisory board. In his time the company grew from 20,000 to 70,000 employees and to sales of 30 billion marks. His successor is Bernd Pischetsrieder rather than the development chief Wolfgang Reitzle.
why: Pischetsrieder's big decision, the purchase of Rover, cost him the job in 1999.
source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eberhard_von_Kuenheim (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernd_Pischetsrieder (read 2026-10-03)

title: Vickers accepts BMW's bid for Rolls-Royce
what: Vickers has accepted BMW's offer for the British luxury car maker Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, which already uses BMW engines; the price is 340 million pounds. Pischetsrieder promised to invest 1 billion pounds, double the workforce and triple production. Volkswagen is preparing a higher offer.
why: VW outbid BMW for the company, but BMW secured the Rolls-Royce name for cars from 2003, the start of its luxury brand. [Lookahead review: 'for now' anticipated the outcome.]
source: BBC News, 'BMW pledges £1bn Rolls-Royce investment', 7 April 1998, http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/71404.stm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Motors (read 2026-10-03)

title: Rover's troubles deepen
what: Rover keeps losing money and market share in Britain. The pound has climbed above 3 marks, which makes Rover's British-built cars far more costly for BMW, and Rover's future is openly questioned in the British press, which puts off buyers. BMW is considering a strategic change of course.
why: -26%; the market priced in a costly exit. DaimlerChrysler fell 16% the same month, so part of it was a flight from old-economy shares in the dot-com boom. BMW announced the break-up of Rover six weeks later.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 1999, preface by Joachim Milberg, https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_1999.pdf (read 2026-10-03); BBC News, 'Rover - a car firm's troubles', 29 October 1999, http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/353271.stm (read 2026-10-03); data/out/mercedes.json (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW breaks up Rover and the shares jump
what: On 16 March BMW announced that it is giving up Rover. Rover Cars and the Longbridge plant go to the British investor Alchemy Partners, with BMW paying to be rid of them; Land Rover is to be sold to Ford, reportedly for 1.8 billion pounds. BMW keeps the Cowley plant near Oxford to build the new Mini. A one-off charge of 3.15 billion euros produced a net loss of 2.49 billion euros for 1999.
why: Relief: +23% in a month. The Alchemy deal later fell through and Rover went to the Phoenix consortium for a nominal 10 pounds; Ford paid 1.8 billion pounds for Land Rover.
source: BBC News, 'BMW splits up Rover', 17 March 2000, http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/679169.stm (read 2026-10-03); BMW Group Annual Report 1999, https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_1999.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (16 March 2000, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rover_Group (read 2026-10-03)

title: The new Mini goes on sale
what: BMW's new Mini, built at the former Morris plant in Cowley, Oxford, went on sale in July. It is the first new car of BMW's 'premium only' strategy after the sale of Rover and Land Rover: a small car sold at a high price on the strength of a famous name.
why: The Mini was an immediate success and became, with Rolls-Royce from 2003, the proof that BMW had kept the right part of Rover.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_(marque) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Helmut Panke succeeds Milberg
what: Helmut Panke, who used to run BMW's American business, became chairman of BMW in May, succeeding Joachim Milberg, who stepped down for health reasons.
why: The Panke years (2002-2006) were BMW's steady growth phase.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Panke (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joachim_Milberg (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW builds its first Rolls-Royce
what: From 1 January only BMW may call cars 'Rolls-Royce'. Its new subsidiary Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, with a new plant at Goodwood in the south of England, is launching the Phantom saloon. Volkswagen keeps the old Crewe factory and the Bentley brand.
why: BMW now covers the market from the Mini to the grandest luxury saloons.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Motors (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Motor_Cars (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW opens its first car plant in China
what: BMW and its Chinese partner Brilliance officially opened a new car plant in Shenyang in northern China in May. BMW is also having a record year: it has launched the X3, the 6 Series and new 5 Series models and will launch a compact car, the 1 Series, in September.
why: The start of the China story: China became one of BMW's most important markets, and its slump in 2024-2026 was BMW's biggest problem.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2004 (Shenyang plant officially opened in May 2004; model launches), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2004.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (read 2026-10-03)

title: Norbert Reithofer takes the wheel
what: Norbert Reithofer succeeded Helmut Panke as chairman of BMW on 1 September.
why: Reithofer steered BMW through the financial crisis and started the electric 'i' cars.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Reithofer (read 2026-10-03)

title: Reithofer's 'Number ONE' strategy
what: At the end of September BMW announced a new strategy called Number ONE: it wants to sell more than two million cars a year by 2020, remain the leading premium car maker, invest in new technologies and drive systems, and raise profitability.
why: The plan was barely announced when the financial crisis hit; it later led to the electric 'i' cars.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2007 ('Strategic realignment of the BMW Group announced'), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2007.pdf (read 2026-10-03)

title: Record sales and cheap ECB money lift BMW
what: BMW sold a record 1,668,982 BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce cars in 2011, and Rolls-Royce reported record sales on Asian demand. Fears about the eurozone have eased since the European Central Bank lent banks 489 billion euros for three years at 1% on 22 December, and BMW shares rose 27% in January.
why: +27% in a month, a rebound from the autumn lows of the euro crisis.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2011 (deliveries 2011), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2011.pdf (read 2026-10-03); The Guardian, 'Rolls-Royce hits new sales record on Asian demand', 9 January 2012 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_debt_crisis (LTRO, read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW's first electric car, the i3, is on the road
what: BMW has launched the i3 this year, its first series-built battery electric car and the first model of its new 'i' brand for electric cars, which chief executive Norbert Reithofer has pushed.
why: The start of BMW's electric era (the 2-millionth BMW electric car followed in 2026). The month is not confirmed; the sources give only the year 2013.
source: AutoBuzz.my, 'BMW just delivered its 2 millionth EV after 13 years', 7 September 2026, https://autobuzz.my/2026/09/07/bmw-just-delivered-its-2-millionth-ev-after-13-years/ (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Reithofer (read 2026-10-03)

title: Harald Krüger named as Reithofer's successor
what: BMW said on 9 December that board member Harald Krüger will become chief executive in May 2015, succeeding Norbert Reithofer, who is to move to the chairmanship of the supervisory board.
why: Krüger (2015-2019) took over just before the diesel scandal; in his time Mercedes overtook BMW as the best-selling luxury brand.
source: bmwblog, 'Harald Krüger to become BMW's CEO in May 2015', 9 December 2014, https://www.bmwblog.com/2014/12/09/harald-kruger-become-bmws-ceo-may-2015/ (via Google News, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Reithofer (read 2026-10-03)

title: The diesel scandal reaches BMW
what: After Volkswagen admitted cheating on diesel emissions tests, the German magazine Auto Bild reported on 24 September that a diesel BMW X3 emitted 11 times the European limit for nitrogen oxides in a road test. BMW denied any manipulation, but its shares fell almost 10% that day. The new chief executive Harald Krüger, in office since May, collapsed on stage at a news conference in Frankfurt on 15 September; BMW said it was not serious.
why: BMW kept denying the report, and the shares rebounded in October (+17%).
source: CBC News, 'BMW disputes report its diesel X3 also failed emissions test', 24 September 2015, https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/volkswagen-emissions-bmw-1.3241472 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harald_Krüger (read 2026-10-03)

title: Britain votes to leave the EU
what: In the referendum of 23 June, 51.9% of British voters chose to leave the European Union. BMW builds the Mini in Oxford and Rolls-Royce at Goodwood.
why: -14% in the month; Brexit hung over the Mini plant in Oxford for years.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brexit (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_(marque) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Cartel allegations against German car makers
what: Reports in July said that German car makers, BMW among them, had coordinated technology, costs and suppliers in secret working groups for years, including on diesel exhaust cleaning. BMW denied colluding on emissions equipment.
why: Part of the long diesel overhang on German car shares.
source: The New York Times, 'BMW Denies Colluding With Carmakers on Emissions Equipment', 23 July 2017 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); Bloomberg, 'German Carmakers Can't Catch a Break as Next Scandal Looms Large', 21 July 2017 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Oliver Zipse named chief executive
what: On 5 July BMW said Harald Krüger will not seek a second term, and on 18 July the supervisory board named the production chief Oliver Zipse as the new chairman of the board of management from 16 August. Mercedes has overtaken BMW as the best-selling luxury brand.
why: Zipse (2019-2026) steered BMW through COVID and the electric transition, and handed over just as the China slump hit.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harald_Krüger (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Zipse (read 2026-10-03)

title: War in Ukraine and chip shortages cut BMW's forecast
what: BMW doubled its pre-pandemic profit in 2021 thanks to record sales and high prices. On 16 March it cut its margin forecast for 2022 to 7-9% from 8-10%, because Russia's invasion of Ukraine has disrupted the supply of parts such as wire harnesses, on top of the shortage of chips.
why: The record-profit years of 2021-2022 came from scarce cars and high prices; they did not last.
source: City A.M., 'BMW cuts 2022 profit margins as Ukraine war worsens supply chain issues', 16 March 2022, https://www.cityam.com/bmw-cuts-2022-profit-margins-ukraine-war-worsens-supply-chain-issues/ (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW shows the 'Neue Klasse'
what: At the IAA motor show in Munich BMW unveiled the Vision Neue Klasse, a concept for its next generation of electric cars, to be built mainly in a new plant in Debrecen, Hungary, with the first models due around 2025.
why: The bet that was to carry BMW into the electric age; its first model, the iX3, was presented in 2025.
source: bmwblog, 'BMW Vision Neue Klasse Makes Debut at IAA 2023', 6 September 2023, https://www.bmwblog.com/2023/09/06/bmw-vision-neue-klasse-iaa-2023/ (via Google News, read 2026-10-03); BMW Group press release on the iX3 at IAA Mobility 2025 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Brake recall and China force a profit warning
what: On 10 September BMW recalled more than 1.5 million cars because of a faulty brake component from the supplier Continental and stopped deliveries of 320,000 cars not yet handed over. Together with weak demand in China, the recall made BMW cut its profit forecast for 2024, and the shares plunged.
why: The first of the warnings of the China slump years.
source: DW, 'BMW recalls 1.5 million cars over brake issue', 10 September 2024, https://www.dw.com/en/bmw-recalls-15-million-cars-over-brake-issue/a-70182052 (read 2026-10-03); Reuters, 'BMW cuts 2024 outlook on Continental brake issues, shares plunge', 10 September 2024 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Milan Nedeljković becomes BMW's chief executive
what: At the annual general meeting on 13 May, Oliver Zipse handed over the chairmanship of the board of management to Milan Nedeljković, until now the board member for production.
why: The new chief starts with job cuts in a crisis year.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (list of chairmen, BMW Group press release of 13 May 2026, read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW warns of a 'significant' profit fall
what: On 16 June BMW cut its forecast for 2026: it now expects a significant fall in pre-tax profit and a car margin of only 1 to 3%, down from 4 to 6%, because the Chinese market is shrinking faster than expected under strong local competition and the war with Iran keeps energy costs high and weighs on demand. The shares fell to their lowest level since 2020.
why: -25% in June, one of BMW's worst months; it also pulled down Mercedes. BMW paid its dividend in May, so the fall is not a dividend effect.
source: Yahoo Finance, 'BMW warns of significant profit decline as shares fall 7%', 17 June 2026, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bmw-warns-significant-profit-decline-104414505.html (read 2026-10-03); Reuters, 'BMW shares sink after profit warning highlights China and Iran risk', 17 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); data/out/bmw.json (dividend in May 2026) (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW at a six-year low before its strategy day
what: BMW shares fell to their lowest since 2020 in September, down about 40% this year. At its capital markets day on 30 September the new chief executive Nedeljković promised a car margin of 3 to 5% by 2028 and 8 to 10% in the early 2030s, with a simpler model range, cheaper local parts and fewer dealers in China; about 8,000 jobs have already been cut. Some investors had hoped for more, but analysts called it the beginning of a healing process.
why: -14% in September. The arc ends with BMW, like Mercedes, struggling to replace lost Chinese profits.
source: MarketScreener, 'BMW Investors' Nervousness Over Capital Markets Day Statements Eases', 30 September 2026, https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bmw-investors-nervousness-over-capital-markets-day-statements-eases-ce785ad2dd8ef024 (read 2026-10-03); Yahoo Finance Singapore, 'BMW plans margin rebuild with simpler line-up and pricier cars', https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/bmw-plans-margin-rebuild-simpler-041200536.html (read 2026-10-03); Investing.com, 'BMW stock hits a fresh 6-year low ahead of next week's CMD', 24 September 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
